title: Pat McAfee addresses growing ESPN role amid recent backlash
description: Pat McAfee is inescapable right now. On Friday he released his debut album. Yesterday came the news that he would be joining ESPN’s “Monday Night Countdown.” Today Andrew Marchand reported that McAfee was also close to an agreement to do…
fullText:
Pat McAfee is inescapable right now. On Friday he released his debut album. Yesterday came the news that he would be joining ESPN's "Monday Night Countdown." Today Andrew Marchand reported that McAfee was also close to an agreement to do a "Monday Night Football" alt-cast whenever the "ManningCast" is dark.

McAfee posted about the news on Wednesday, saying how honored he was just to be involved with "Countdown. He also called himself the "luckiest man on Earth." Via X:

MORE: 'First Take' tribute to Bill Rasmussen abruptly interrupted by 'Pat McAfee Show'

'Tis an honor to be a part of MNF in any capacity. I hope I can be an asset as we start the journey to The Biggest Super Bowl of all time in LA on ESPN and ABC

College GameDay on Saturday.. Monday Night Countdown on Monday.. I'm the luckiest man on Earth. Football has been so good to me and my family.. I will try my best to continue to give back to it.

We started this show in the basement.. no agent.. no publicist.. no manager.. no PR firm.. just a love of sport and it's people. So thankful for it all and for all of you who have followed along with this absurdly dumb life.

MORE: Best & Worst from Pat McAfee's 'Diary of a Polarizing Figure' album

McAfee's album title suggests that he is a polarizing figure, but at ESPN, there seems to be a consensus that the more McAfee, the better. Football is the most popular sport. McAfee is now featured prominently on Saturday and Monday on the network's two biggest pregame shows. He also occupies two hours from noon to 2 p.m. ET every single day of the work week.

What more can you say about his place at ESPN? He has replaced Stephen A. Smith as the face of network. He was first recruited to join their Thursday college football coverage in 2019. When they decided to bring his whole show to ESPN in 2023 the Wall Street Journal called him an "F-bomb throwing YouTube star."

While you still may hear the occasional F-bomb on ESPN, the shock is gone. He may have just released a country-rap fusion album, but he is clearly corporate rock. And he's playing on every channel.

title: US Open offers biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history
description: The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year.
fullText:
The US Open will offer the biggest prize fund in Grand Slam history with a total of $108 million (£79.2m) on offer - marking a 20% increase on last year.

The singles' champions will receive $5.5m (£4.03m) each in a 10% increase on 2025.

First-round losers will take home $140,000 (£102,667) - which is $30,000 and 27% more than last year.

The prize pool includes a $2m (£1.47m) contribution to a welfare fund, which leading players have been demanding from all the Grand Slams.

The four Grand Slam tournaments have also jointly announced the formation of a Grand Slam Player Council. This was another key request from players, some of who limited media appearances at the French Open and Wimbledon to 15 minutes to highlight their grievances.

Their other main demand is for each Grand Slam to dedicate 16% of its revenue to prize money, with the figure rising to 22% by 2030.

It is possible the US Open has become the first Slam to hit that target, but the US Tennis Association (USTA) has not yet published its financial statement for 2025.

Alcaraz to play US Open after four months out

Player representatives have also not seen the figures. However, if you allow for 10% growth to the $559.7m (£410.5m) the US Open generated in revenue in 2024, then prize money of $98.5m would have be in line with player expectations.

The USTA says the financial statement will be published before the start of the main draw.

Chief executive Craig Tiley, who previously headed up Tennis Australia, described the offer as "a significant first step in a multi-year investment in athletes".

In a BBC interview in March, world number three Jessica Pegula highlighted how last year's US Open increase was targeted primarily at those who needed it least -the players who made the second week.

This year, however, the percentage increase is highest in the first round, then falls in every subsequent round.

There are also greater rewards for those competing in the mixed doubles event, which takes place during qualifying week.

The winners will still share $1m, but there is more for everyone else who enters, with first-round prize money doubled.

Player representatives had asked each Grand Slam to contribute $4m in benefit payments this year. The USTA is the first to ring-fence this money for the players, but it will come out of the overall prize fund.

The money for the new US Open player support programme will be placed in an independent holding account while the details are worked through.

The Grand Slam Player Council will have input into this. It will launch after the US Open "with a focus on player input into sporting matters at the four Grand Slam tournaments".

The exact framework is yet to be decided, but players have been invited to apply and told the council will allow them to discuss specific prize money concerns directly with the Grand Slam in question.

Player representatives "welcomed" the various announcements and noted the "substantial increase" in prize money.

"Players look forward to building on today's positive announcements and ensuring the Council develops into a genuinely representative and effective forum for player consultation, while continuing to work through their representatives on prize money and player welfare," a statement read.

The US Open begins on Sunday, 30 August.

title: Deon Thomas praises Brad Underwood and Illinois’ recent success
description: Thomas isn’t taking Underwood for granted.
fullText:
Illinois basketball's all-time leading scorer, Deon Thomas, hopped on The Champaign Room podcast with Isaac Ambrose and Ethan Pavey to touch on head coach Brad Underwood's recent success and highlight the bright future of Illinois athletics.

Deon Thomas joins the show! 🏀🎙️@deonthomas25 joins @IMAbrose & @TheEthanTalk to give his thoughts on Brad Underwood's success, his favorite #Illini memories as a player, and the future of Illinois Athletics https://t.co/CoXWVZQFtg

Thomas emphasized the importance of last season's Final Four run, noting that he himself had never been past the second round of the NCAA Tournament with the Fighting Illini. Now serving as Illinois athletics' director of major gifts and radio color analyst, Thomas saw firsthand just how much that meant to his department.

"I know how important that was to, not just the coaches or the players themselves, but to the department which I'm a part of right now, and to Illini nation as a whole," Thomas said.

Thomas noted that while Illinois has been regarded as one of collegiate basketball's historically elite programs, the past few decades lacked milestones to back that claim up. But the Underwood era of success and eventual accomplishment of reaching the Final Four sent the message to the NCAA that the Illini are back in the conversation that they belong in, and the crowd of orange at Lucas Oil Stadium made it clear that the fans were starving for it.

In this rapidly changing era of college basketball, Underwood has consistently kept Illinois afloat during his nine-season tenure, and Thomas gave some insight into how he does it.

"Brad has an open mindedness about himself that allows him to look at situations and figure out solutions," Thomas said. "His flexibility from a coaching standpoint, utilizing and learning from and understanding the staff that he has brought in, and making adjustments when he has had to has really helped, not just Illinois basketball, but I think his personal growth."

Thomas didn't hesitate to show his appreciation for Brad Underwood and what he's done for this program, putting Underwood's growth hand in hand with the team's success.

"As he grows, the team grows. Look at where we are right now," Thomas said. "Here we are a decade later, and he's been shining for us."

With Illinois retaining a large portion of its Final Four squad, both Illini fans and Deon Thomas expect that momentum to carry over into next season. Thomas highlighted how having multiple veteran voices in the locker room helps new additions adapt quickly.

"What that does is, it cuts down the learning time," Thomas said. "When you're able to bring back pieces that can help the younger players or new players understand what you're expecting from them, the older players or returning players can help them learn the system and help them groom and grow faster."

With a veteran core returning, fresh talent settling in and a stampede of orange and blue backing Underwood as he carries the torch into next season, who says no to another Final Four run for Illinois?

title: Dalot And Mbeumo To Start | 4-2-3-1 Manchester United Predicted Lineup Vs Hull City

fullText:
Manchester United will face off against Hull City at the MKM Stadium on Saturday as they look to secure a win in their Premier League opener. The Red Devils suffered a 4-2 defeat at the hands of AC Milan in a pre-season game earlier this month, which has halted their momentum somewhat going into this clash.

Michael Carrick will opt for the 4-2-3-1 formation and is expected to make some changes to his first-team for this game. Both Diogo Dalot and Bryan Mbeumo could get a chance to impress from the start of this contest.

Senne Lammens will feature in goal for the Red Devils after conceding four goals in his last pre-season outing. Harry Maguire will function alongside Ayden Heaven at the heart of the Man United backline as they look to keep a good shape on the defensive end of the field.

Diogo Dalot will try to catch the eye as the right-back, while Luke Shaw hopes to shine on the other side as the left-back. Both of them will get the license to go forward and express themselves inside the opponent's half.

Lisandro Martinez and Noussair Mazraoui will offer cover for the defensive positions on the bench.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans will anchor the midfield for the Mancunian club as they try to win the 50-50 battles at the centre of the park. The talented trio of Patrick Dorgu, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo will operate just ahead of them as part of Carrick's attack. All three of them need to combine well if Man United want to secure all three points at the MKM this weekend.

Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford will have to settle for a place on the bench as they wait for their chance to influence the game in the second 45 minutes if needed.

Bryan Mbeumo will lead the line for the Mancunian club in the final third. He has to find a way to be a constant menace up top.

Benjamin Sesko is unlikely to recover in time for this game. However, Matheus Cunha and Joshua Zirkzee will be available for selection on the bench and might come on to make an impact in the latter stages of the game if required.

title: Rory McIlroy Calls Out Phil Mickelson for ‘Blowing’ Up Golf When He Led Exodus from PGA Tour
description: McIlroy, a six-time major champ, has been a longtime critic of LIV Golf
fullText:
Rory McIlroy is continuing to speak out against LIV Golf

The golfer referenced Phil Mickelson in his criticism of the breakaway tour on Wednesday, Aug. 19

The final LIV Golf tournament of the season begins on Thursday, Aug. 20 in Indiana

In his latest round of critical comments aimed at LIV Golf, Rory McIlroy is questioning Phil Mickelson's impact on the breakaway tour.

"Yeah, were there some things at the start of LIV that the PGA Tour could have done better? Sure," McIlroy, 37, told reporters on Wednesday, Aug. 19, ahead of the BMW Championship. "But I think that, you know, the guys that went, or you look, you think back to the start with, like, say, Phil was unhappy with some stuff or whatever it was."

He continued, "Like, surely that just warranted a conversation instead of blowing the entire professional game up and doing something else."

Mickelson was among golf's most notable names who jumped to LIV in 2022, along with Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson. The 56-year-old golfer, who has been under fire following allegations of misconduct, stepped away from the sport in recent months after announcing he was dealing with a "family health matter."

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — 

LIV continues to evolve amid financial issues, with the final tournament of the season getting underway on Thursday, Aug. 20 at The Club at Chatham Hills in Westfield, Indiana.

Should LIV return next year, it is expected to have 10 events on the schedule and permit players to contend on other tours, ESPN reported.

McIlroy has questioned the value of a potential reunion with his former tour mates.

"I mean, I would argue, have they brought value to LIV?" McIlroy said. "I think the PGA Tour's in a really good spot."

He continued, "I feel like I've kept my position consistent that LIV has never been a good thing for the game. Whatever [LIV] 2.0 looks like — if it even happens — they're saying they're trying to be more collaborative and all of that, but this is the best platform for the top professional golfers in the world."

McIlroy, who previously served as a player director on the PGA Tour Policy Board, has long believed it is his duty to "protect the PGA Tour" — and hasn't pulled punches about his standing.

"I still hate LIV," he said in 2023. "I hope it goes away and I fully expect that it does and I think that's where the distinction here is," he said. "All I've tried to do is protect what the PGA Tour is and what the PGA Tour stands for, and I think it will continue to do that."

title: Andy Reid reveals injury updates before Saturday's preseason game
description: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid shared the latest injury updates ahead of Saturday's preseason game | @EdEastonJr
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid spoke with reporters after practice on Thursday at Missouri Western State University. He shared the latest injury updates ahead of Saturday's preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"So, as far as injuries go, Jack Cochrane and (Chamarri) Connor tried it today. We backed them off. They will not play. (Jeff) Caldwell, with his hyperextended knee, won't play. (Ashton) Gillotte has a plantar fascia that ruptured. He won't play. (Jimmy) Holiday won't play, and (Josh) Simmons and Trey (Smith) won't play on the offensive line. The rest of the guys will get up and have an opportunity to get out there and do some things."

Mahomes was officially ruled out as well, with Reid deciding to stick with the same three quarterback rotation from the first preseason game. He explained two players are being held out for safety precautions before the start of the regular season.

"Yeah, (Ashton Gillotte and Josh Simmons) they're not—these aren't like extended injuries. They'll be back in, just nicks and bruises type thing. So, they're working through them, and they'll be back in and going," said Reid (Trey Smith). He's making progress, so yeah."

The Chiefs will travel to Tampa Bay for the second preseason game as players on the bubble continue to compete for a roster spot.

title: Where do Red Wings stand in GM search? One inside source sheds light
description: The Detroit Red Wings are embedded in a search for a new hockey operations leader, whose first task will be sorting out the Dylan Larkin situation.
fullText:
The Detroit Red Wings are embedded in a search for a new hockey operations leader, whose first task will be sorting out the Dylan Larkin situation.

Right now − in the middle of August − Wings owner Chris Ilitch is holding the cards in charge of the Wings.

The Red Wings and former general manager Steve Yzerman parted ways on July 15 after the Red Wings missed the playoffs for a 10th straight year, seventh under Yzerman since he was named GM in April 2019.

So the Red Wings have gone more than a month without a GM, but the team is dedicated in taking its time to make the right call on who is next.

"From the very beginning, we were never going to let the process or the timeline dictate" the decision on whom to hire, a person with knowledge of the Detroit Red Wings' organizational thinking told the Detroit Free Press. "We're always going to really be super thorough. I can tell you that when we moved on from Steve, we did it really strategically.

"People forget that right around the Olympic break, we were not only contending for a playoff berth, we were in first place. So it's hard to say, hey, Monday morning quarterback, why didn't you do this in April? And the real reason is because we didn't want to make knee-jerk decisions, we want to be super thorough."

As the Free Press was the first to report, the Red Wings have hired a search firm (TurnkeyZRG) to help narrow their search for who will replace Yzerman.

"We spent our time to really understand what's the right thing for the Red Wings moving forward to win the Stanley Cup − that's the only thing that matters," the source said. "I can tell you that there is no one that cares more about that than Chris, and there's no one that works harder in our building than Chris Illich achieving that among other goals that he has. So when we moved on from Steve, and when we made that announcement, it wasn't just on a whim, it was because we were really thoughtful about it."

The Wings brought Yzerman in in spring of 2019, as someone who could turn around the franchise. At that time, the Wings had ended a historic 25-season streak of making the the playoffs in 2017.

But after recent seasons fell short of expectations, the Red Wings decided to go in another direction to reach their ultimate destination − deep in the playoffs.

"Chris challenged [everyone], let's go find the next leader that's going to bring a Stanley Cup to Detroit, from whatever level they're at in the organization that they're with right now," the source said. "Let's go find that person. And so we started with over 100 names. And we are making our way methodically through that in a manner where we're being strategic, trying to figure out how do we get the right person in the role?

"I'm not going to comment on specifics on where we're at and interview process or timeline because I don't want to paint a picture that, you know, we have a specific date. Yes, we'd like to have somebody in by training camp. But at the end of the day, what people should feel really confident in is that we're turning over every stone and going through a very thorough strategic process."

As for the Larkin situation, the Wings do not want to trade him without getting full value in return. And that could well mean Larkin will be in a Red Wings jersey when camp starts September 17.

Larkin, 30, requested a trade shortly after the season ended. He has five years left on a contract carrying an $8.7 million cap hit. Larkin has not responded to requests for comment and his agent has declined comment, too.

Contact Helene St. James at Hstjames@freepress.com.

title: Thomas ton helps Somerset start strongly v Essex
description: Josh Thomas scores a century and New Zealand's Henry Nicholls hits 96 on debut as Somerset start well against Essex.
fullText:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, The Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton (day one)

Somerset 348-5: Thomas 110, Nicholls 96, Abell 65; Snater 2-68

Bonus points: Somerset 2pts, Essex 1pt

Josh Thomas posted an eye-catching hundred as title-chasing Somerset assumed a position of strength on the opening day of the County Championship Division One match against Essex at the Cooper Associates Ground.

Taunton-born Thomas scored 110 from 162 balls, struck 15 fours and a six and dominated a stand of 119 for the third wicket with new overseas signing Henry Nicholls, who made 96 on debut as Somerset raised 348-5 after being put in to bat.

Tom Abell also weighed in with 65 and helped add 99 for the fourth wicket with Nicholls, while James Rew finished on 21 not out.

Sam Cook and Shane Snater proved the pick of the Essex bowlers, claiming 2-77 and 2-68 respectively on a day of toil for the seamers.

Visiting skipper Tom Westley may already be regretting his decision to insert the opposition on an essentially docile surface.

Although Thomas has been a permanent fixture at the top of Somerset's order this season, he has had six different opening partners. The latest permutation featured Tom Lammonby, whose stay in the middle was cut short by devilish misfortune.

There appeared to be no danger when Cook directed a delivery down leg-side, only for the ball to snag on the underside of Lammonby's thigh pad and deflect onto his stumps.

Lewis Goldsworthy will also have been disappointed by the manner of his dismissal, the Cornishman pursuing a delivery outside off stump from Jamie Porter and presenting Michael Pepper with an opportunity to take a diving catch in front of first slip with the score 94-2. At least the hitherto watchful Goldsworthy had contributed 16 in a progressive alliance of 60 for the second wicket before taking his leave.

Unaffected by events at the other end, Thomas survived an early examination against the swinging new ball to raise a fluent half-century from 75 deliveries with eight boundaries.

He found a willing ally in new overseas recruit Nicholls, the New Zealand Test batter sweeping to good effect against Simon Harmer's spin as the home side reached lunch well placed on 134-2.

In need of a wicket, Essex were left to rue their profligacy when Harmer found the edge and Pepper put down a chance to hand Nicholls a life on 43. Somerset made them pay, the third-wicket pair raising a hundred partnership via 185 balls.

Cutting and driving fluently when the opportunity presented itself, Thomas also demonstrated solid defence and sound temperament as he closed in on his second first-class hundred, a landmark attained off 148 deliveries when he carved Harmer away behind point.

Proving the perfect foil, the obdurate Nicholls went to a patient 50 from 120 balls with his eighth four, shortly before Snater bowled Thomas to claim the wicket an improved afternoon bowling performance warranted. Providing reassurance thereafter, Nicholls and Abell advanced the score to 248-3 at tea.

Harmer bowled better than his figures suggested on a surface offering only occasional assistance to spin, but Nicholls and Abell looked increasingly secure on their way to collecting two batting bonus points during the final session.

Uncomplicated in his approach, Nicholls endeared himself to the Taunton regulars long before he was out four runs short of what would have been a crowd-pleasing hundred. Taking the new ball with Essex backs against the wall, Cook induced the Kiwi to chop on with the score 313-4.

Thereafter, Abell ensured Somerset further improved their position. Back in harness after injury and making his first Championship appearance since May, he played with increasing assurance in crafting a chanceless half-century from 81 balls.

Snater produced a beauty to bowl him shortly before the close, but Somerset could be thoroughly satisfied with their day's work.

title: Aaron Donald risks tarnishing his legacy if he stays retired
description: If Donald stays retired and then goes on a promotional tour, he risks alienating his fan base
fullText:
As Aaron Donald continues to tease fans with indirect hints that he's working towards a comeback with the Los Angeles Rams, he also risks alienating and frustrating those same people who believe he's returning if he later announces that he's going to stay retired. Even if it's his right to make an attempt, and even if he's being genuine in his interest to come back, it's been nearly three months of speculation already — that he's fueled himself — and Rams fans are expressing a contempt for seeing Aaron Donald's name in the news that we've never seen before.

If Donald comes back, then he's a hero. If he doesn't though, some Rams fans will feel they've been used.

I'm to the point where I feel the need to mute the words "Aaron Donald" on this app until after this does or does not happen. https://t.co/g02LdpKrtR

On June 1, 2026, Donald made an Instagram post of him working out with the hashtag "#ready" that many people ran with as an indication that he's on the precipice of making a return announcement. Ironically, we've since had 10 weeks of Aaron Donald headlines that make it clear, "He'll only come back when he's ready."

So…I guess he wasn't #ready then?

No, in fact, that's not even why Donald used that hashtag, which some of you already know. Maybe it's the fact that most Rams fans don't know why he used the word "ready" that has inspired this many headlines about Aaron Donald to be created.

Ready is the name of his protein bar and sports drink franchise.

In one of the most electric interviews of all-time, Donald reveals that his favorite Ready protein bar is…chocolate peanut butter!

On June 2, one day after his #ready post, that's when Pat McAfee goes on his show and tells the world that he texted Donald and that the Myles Garrett trade has "got me thinking" about a return.

Who would ever accuse McAfee of being brand-focused and financially motivated?

You wake up and open Draft Kings. You hammer the Pat McAfee featured parlay just like normal. You turn on ESPN and watch Pat McAfee debate AI Pat McAfee. During the 16 straight commercials you play the new McAfee album. Banger. You DoorDash the new Pat McAfee meal.

Life is good.

But to be fair, Donald hasn't say much about Ready since June 1, and really he hasn't said anything at all. If this were to promote his brand, he's doing a very bad job at it. Donald isn't speaking to the media, he's not taking interviews, he's not going on podcasts, which are all things he could be doing with his name in the news every day. Certainly an Aaron Donald appearance on McAfee this week would get millions of views even if he didn't want to talk about coming out of retirement.

That's how much interest there is around him right now.

So we can assume that Donald's training, and his two official workouts with the Rams when he used their facilities in an official capacity, are all genuine efforts to see if he can play and maybe get a second Super Bowl ring.

This still wouldn't stop the fact that many Rams fans are getting tired of news about a player who isn't on the team and who they fear still won't be when all these rumors stop.

In a recent Feed post by our own John Newman, "Do you think Donald is serious?", many fans talked about Donald in a way that I've never heard Rams fans talk about Aaron Donald before.

Here are some of the top comments:

SlowTightEnd: "Actually, I don't think he's serious. And, I think it's an unnecessary distraction for the team. Frankly, AD was seriously injured in that 2022 fiasco season and missed a lot of games. Then he was good in 2023, but not his former sensational self. I sure wish we'd had him in 2024 and 2025. Especially the latter year where just another sack or two versus Sam Darnold would've likely meant a SB Championship. But after two years off and at age 35, no $30M payday please."

And I'm not highlighting any of your comments to disparage fans or Donald. This is just how many people are starting to feel and let's call a spade a spade: It's fascinating and unexpected.

Ramaha: "At this point I don't really care. The Rams don't need him. This is an asinine luxury. Play or don't. Think the Rams players are tired as hell about questions about AD. At what point does he become a distraction?"

What was once a fun idea has now become an unwelcome distraction.

Rams62: "If he isn't serious about coming back then I think this is lousy and cheap way to get some attention."

And therein lies the heart of the problem if Donald doesn't come out of retirement. Even if it's just because he tried and decided he doesn't have the juice anymore, perception is reality. Many will feel duped.

ohramsfan: "I think since it was disclosed he has a production group in place for a possible documentary, that's all this is, meaning promotion for his yet to be filmed documentary… I hope he proves me wrong, but the longer it goes the less I believe him returning."

If an AD documentary does get released in the future, detailing these months, it could do more harm than good. Just another fake reality show?

Tom House: "He's like a week away from slightly tarnishing his otherwise impeccable legacy. Only 'cause indecision makes you look weak."

This comment was 3 days ago, so the clock is ticking on the decision.

Although Aaron Donald tarnishing his legacy with Rams fans would be like Tom Cruise tarnishing his legacy with the Church of Scientology (meaning there's almost no wrong that can be done), he's still going from infallible to fallible the longer this drags out.

Maybe Donald just doesn't want to be added to the roster yet. It could behoove the team to wait until after final cuts.

But these reports could have stayed in the shadows. Sean McVay could have refused to talk about Donald to the media, and instead he is surprisingly candid about it and happy to receive questions that aren't actually about the team. That feels a little unusual and perhaps he's too elated to talk about Donald. Does he know the outcome already?

If Aaron Donald announces his return this month, his reputation with Rams fans will go above heights we ever thought was possible. Even if he's not his old self, fans will appreciate the effort.

However, if Donald stays retired, and then goes on McAfee and promotes Ready protein bars, and releases a documentary about his attempt to return, his legacy will take a hit that we've never seen before.

title: Mike Norvell gives injury update for FSU
description: Mike Norvell provides an injury update as FSU is in the final week of fall camp.
fullText:
The Florida State Seminoles are wrapping up fall camp this week ahead of their Week Zero matchup with the New Mexico State Aggies on Aug. 29 in Doak Campbell Stadium.

While he acknowledged that losing defensive back Karson Hobbs for the season is a major blow, head coach Mike Norvell is pleased with the overall health of the team.

"Losing Karson was a big hit for us," he said. "I was really excited about what I was expecting from him this year.

"As a whole, I feel good about where we are," he added. "Still a couple things that we'll see as we get in throughout the course this weekend, but I feel good overall."

He mentioned linebacker Mikai Gbayor and wide receiver Jayvan Boggs as two players who returned quicker than expected and are poised to be key contributors.

"Mikai Gbayor and Jayvan Boggs, those guys are getting back, I truly was anticipating that being a game week decision in Week One," Norvell said. "But I think both of those guys have shown that they're going to be fully ready to go. They got cleared to be able to participate. It's been good seeing that push. So getting two guys we expect to be major contributors for us, getting them back a couple weeks early is a great job by our athletic training staff and by those guys in their rehab."

Cornerback Nehemiah Chandler is another player battling for a starting spot that is back playing after being limited earlier in camp.

"He's definitely gonna help this football team this year," Norvell said. "He was a little limited for the last week, and he's just back into full practice yesterday, but I mean he's shown the ability."

Running back Quentrevion Wisner is part of a deep running back room and has been limited, but Norvell is not worried about the veteran.

"He was able to get back in practice here this week," he said. "Feel confident about what that will look like this next week."

Norvell also confirmed that André Otto, who is in the mix to be a starter at right guard, was back practicing.

title: Fantasy Football Busts 2026: Omarion Hampton, Cam Skattebo among Rotoworld's top fades
description: The Rotoworld Football staff uncovers players who carry warning signs headed into fantasy football drafts.
fullText:
Fresh off unveiling our 2026 fantasy football sleepers earlier this week, now it's time for the Rotoworld Football crew to name their "busts" for the season ahead.

Identifying busts is a more difficult task, partially because it's such a loaded term. At the right price, all of the players below are draftable, but whether it's their ADP (average draft position), the situation, or some combination of the two, these are names that come with a certain degree of caution leading into drafts.

Before you join your draft lobby in the coming days, check out the rationale from each of our writers below.

GET YOUR FREE ROTOWORLD FANTASY FOOTBALL DRAFT KIT HERE!

Rotoworld Fantasy Football Draft Central 2026: Rankings, strategy, sleepers, and more

Your one-stop-shop for all of Rotoworld's preseason content leading into fantasy football drafts.

Pierce was reportedly set to diversify his route tree when the front office signed him to a lucrative extension this offseason. Instead of learning the nuances required for short-to-intermediate-depth usage, Pierce has been sidelined by a nagging ankle injury which required surgery and at least one PRP injection. At best, Pierce will remain stuck in his one-dimensional role, out of shape and earning targets thrown by a quarterback, Daniel Jones, whose driving back leg experienced a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture last year. - Nic Bodiford

Hampton last year was 65th out of 70 qualifying running backs in success rate on zone rushes, which new Chargers offensive coordinator McDaniel favors as part of the Shanahan system. Hampton ranked 68th out of 70 backs in yards per carry on 125 zone rushes last year. He's a poor fit for the Shanny scheme and the addition of Keaton Mitchell could prove to be just enough of a problem to make Hampton a bust once again. - Denny Carter

Skattebo had a high-volume rookie season that was inefficient and shortened by an ankle dislocation and fibula fracture. He tallied -0.13 EPA per rush last season; among running backs with at least 100 carries, he ranked outside the top 25 in yards per carry, success rate, and explosive rate. For 2026, Skattebo isn't as well-equipped to handle a large workload coming back from last season's injury. Skattebo's contact-seeking playstyle, return from serious injury, and inefficiency make him a fade at his current mid-level RB2 draft range. - Aditya Fuldeore

McLaurin has spent much of his NFL career surrounded by a cast of forgettable receivers. Despite never having another receiver of note push him for targets, McLaurin has finished as the WR20 or lower in PPR points per game in six of his seven seasons in the league, and will now face legit competition from Stefon Diggs for targets. While McLaurin is still expected to operate as the Commanders' WR1, the addition of Diggs, coupled with the fact that he plays with Jayden Daniels, a quarterback who has historically high scramble rates (16.0 percent in 2025, per TruMedia), makes McLaurin a riskier bet than in previous seasons. He's currently being drafted as a low-end WR2, which is how he has produced for most of his career. His ADP may take a slight hit in the coming days, but it may not be enough for McLaurin to provide much value to his fantasy managers. - Zach Krueger

So the Jaguars kept Tuten out of the major reps last year, have an established third-down back in LeQuint Allen, and signed Liam Coen's college crush in Chris Rodriguez for an area in which they definitely want to improve: sustaining power runs. I think there's a non-zero chance Tuten works out this year for managers that draft him as highly as he's going, but there are also a lot of downside paths on this road. I'd rather have Rodriguez of the two at ADP and it isn't close. Ultimately I think the Jaguars will annoy everyone with RBBC and nobody will really be happy here. That isn't anything against Tuten's talent, he's just got the most room to fall here. - Rivers McCown

This one might feel a bit like shooting fish in a barrel since Burden is currently sidelined with a groin injury, but that was already a major concern for this rugged player. Burden plays the game a la Percy Harvin, and it has him limping off the field with disappointing regularity. It cost Burden surprisingly little time at Mizzou, but the gifted wideout was always playing through something. The same was true of his promising rookie year in Chicago. "Injury prone" is a hotly debated concept. If it's real, it is also unknowable. We don't know what makes a player more susceptible to time on the shelf. That's at least true in most cases. My longtime Burden fear is not that he pulls muscles in some sort of systematic fashion, but that he plays the game — read, lots of contact — in a way that lends itself to injury. That, coupled with a loaded young skill corps in an offense that wants to be balanced has me wondering where the requisite target share will come even when he is on the field. The fact that he is already off of it during August does not leave me overflowing with optimism for September and October and beyond. - Patrick Daugherty

Being drafted as the RB8 with an ADP in the teens, Walker is certainly one of the riskier picks on the board. It's the highest price drafters have ever paid for Walker now that he's away from Seattle, where he had to share the backfield. He received a hefty contract from the Chiefs in free agency and the consensus is that Walker will see an expanded role with Patrick Mahomes returning from reconstructive knee surgery. While that's all well and good, this is still the same Chiefs team that routinely leads the league in pass rate over expected and has always used multiple running backs under Andy Reid. Walker himself has never run for 1,100 yards in a season or had 300 receiving yards in a season. He scored 29 touchdowns in four years with the Seahawks while Josh Jacobs has scored 28 in the last two seasons and goes two rounds later. Saquon Barkley, Chase Brown, Derrick Henry, and De'Von Achane should all be easy clicks ahead of Walker. And yet, here we are. - Nick Shlain

Fantasy Football Rankings 2026: Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson headline top 200 overall

Start preparing for your 2026 fantasy football draft with Rotoworld's complete Top 200 overall player rankings.

Moore's numbers have been in freefall for two seasons, bottoming out at 1.1 yards per route in 2025. That came one year after he tumbled to 1.4 YPRR. Per ESPN's player-tracking data, he ranked 50th in Open Score last year and was targeted on a dismal 15 percent of his routes. There's an overwhelming amount of evidence to suggest the Bills' acquisition of Moore could go the way of Amari Cooper as opposed to Stefon Diggs. - Kyle Dvorchak

This one depends on what exactly you think Washington is going to do. He's going off the board right now at WR30 to Brian Thomas', Jakobi Meyers' and Travis Hunter's WR32, WR43 and WR68 respectively. I think it is very important that people are reminded of the fact that Hunter went 8-101-1 on 14 targets before he was lost for the season. He was just starting to heat up. You can feel like Washington is a 1,000-yard receiver, but do it at your own risk if all the Jags' wideouts are healthy. - Lawrence Jackson Jr.

I'm hesitant to call LaPorta a bust because I think he's a really talented football player. I just think he's in an offense loaded with other talented players, and his lengthy injury history makes me nervous at his cost. LaPorta hyperextended his knee in his rookie season, but was able to play through it in the playoffs. He then suffered a sprained AC joint in 2024 and then had a major back injury last season that led to season-ending surgery. The 25-year-old also just suffered a hip injury in Lions' camp, which led to head coach Dan Campbell saying Thursday that he's not sure if he'll be ready for the season. LaPorta could certainly return and stay healthy this season, but it's hard to feel confident about that given his track record so far. Considering his current ADP is 61st overall, ahead of Jadarian Price, Rome Odunze, Christian Watson, and others, I would much rather draft one of the top three tight ends off the board or simply wait for one going later. - Eric Samulski

title: Centennial vs Servite: How to watch California high school football

title: Brian Burns: New York Giants' run defense 'dominant' in practice vs. Miami
description: The New York Giants "dominated" the Miami Dolphins in practice on Thursday, says Brian Burns.
fullText:
Spider-Man is unstoppable these days, not only at the box office, where the Marvel movie is crushing records, but on the field with the New York Giants defense.

But that's not Tom Holland out there in Blue. It's Giants edge rusher Brian Burns, who fancies himself after the iconic superhero. He's crushing it, too.

On Thursday, during a joint practice with the Miami Dolphins at their facility, the Baptist Health Training Center, which is located across the road from Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Burns led a relentless torrent of blue shirts into the opposing backfield.

Brian Burns said the Giants defense was "dominant." They could do better but the Dolphins couldn't stop them. 

Burns was told they had six sacks. He disagreed. He said it was more. pic.twitter.com/dNxcGa9rxX

The Giants have an embarrassment of pass-rushing options this year, so many that stud rookie Arvell Reese is being deployed as an off-ball linebacker rather than on the outside. Burns is the leader of the group that can "get after it."

Abdul Carter, who is on the cusp of possible greatness, mans the opposite flank from Burns. Behind him is veteran Kayvon Thibodeaux. Behind Burns is another very capable vet, Chauncey Golston.

The Dolphins are a rebuilding team under a first-time head coach, Jeff Hafley. They are not expected to win many games this season. They were no match for this group that the Giants general manager Joe Schoen constructed.

Big takeaway in Dolphins-Giants joint practice:

Giants pass rush looks eye-popping dominant. Physical, fast, deep.

Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Arvell Reese — hell of a quartet. They just swarm. Jevón Holland had a strong win with 3rd down sack off edge blitz.

Carter is coming, and Reese is on the tarmac. Burns is the star, though. His peers around the league have taken notice. The 28-year-old has recorded 71.0 sacks in seven seasons in the NFL, with at least 7.5 in each of them.

More are coming from Spider-Man.

title: Carlos Alcaraz to make US Open return after four-month injury layoff
description: The 23-year-old has not played on the ATP Tour since April due to a wrist injury
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz has overcome his fitness struggles and will make his return to competitive tennis at the US Open.

The seven-time grand slam champion has been out of action on the ATP Tour since April due to a persistent wrist injury, choosing to partner with football transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano to announce his impending return.

Alcaraz adopted Romano's signature phrase to confirm he is ready to compete following a four-month layoff.

"Here we go," Alcaraz declared on X, accompanied by an image of the United States flag.

Confirming the news on Instagram, football transfer specialist Romano wrote: "Here we go! Carlos Alcaraz will return to the tour at the US Open after spending four months sidelined with a right wrist injury.

The ongoing wrist problem previously forced the 23-year-old to relinquish his defence of the French Open title and miss Wimbledon, before he also pulled out of the Cincinnati Open at the beginning of August. However, he is now set to feature at Flushing Meadows later this month.

His comeback coincides with the US Open confirming another major rise in prize money for this year's tournament.

A total prize fund of $108m (approximately £80m) stands as the highest ever offered in tennis, reflecting a 20 per cent increase for the second year in succession.

The men's and women's singles champions will take home $5.5m (approximately £4m) each, while players exiting in the first round will receive in excess of £100,000.

Tournament directors hope the historic payout will prevent a repeat of the player protests witnessed at both the French Open and Wimbledon.

A group of high-profile players, including world number ones Jannik Sinner and Aryna Sabalenka, has been involved in a behind-the-scenes dispute with the grand slams under the banner Project RedEye for the past 18 months, raising concerns over prize money and other operational matters.

During the French Open, players limited their pre-tournament media appearances to 15 minutes each and maintained the tactic at Wimbledon, despite benefiting from a 20 per cent increase in overall prize money.

Further action planned for the opening week in London was called off following discussions. Alongside the financial updates from Flushing Meadows, the major tournaments have jointly announced the establishment of a grand slam player advisory council.

Aiming to address player concerns regarding their lack of influence over decision-making, the major tournaments stated that the new panel will act as "the forum for direct communication, feedback and collaboration between the grand slams and players".

The new body will launch after the conclusion of the US Open, which runs from August 30 to September 13, with players invited to submit applications to join.

The council will also serve as a venue to address player welfare, which has formed a core element of recent player dissatisfaction. Furthermore, the US Open's package features a 2m dollars (approximately £1.5m) commitment to a new US Open player support programme.

United States Tennis Association chief executive Craig Tiley, who recently took up the role after leaving Tennis Australia, said: "This is a significant first step in a multi-year investment in athletes as the US Open continues to be the best economic opportunity for players and the most valuable platform in tennis for players, fans and partners.

"We are proud to deliver record-setting prize money and expanded player benefits as well as providing a new platform to work together with players."

Reflecting on the formation of the council, Wimbledon chair Debbie Jevans said: "We have listened to the players' desire for a greater voice and this advisory council is an important step towards a stronger relationship between the grand slams and the players.

"We look forward to working together to elevate the player experience, further enhance the grand slam tournaments and ensure the sport continues to thrive."

title: Jason Beck says Bryce Underwood has strung together 13 good practices
description: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood is showing steady improvement and consistency during fall camp practices.
fullText:
There are high expectations for Michigan football quarterback Bryce Underwood, but few expect him to actually improve upon his freshman year. And yet, it appears he's doing just that.

Last Wednesday, the Big Ten Network took in a practice in Ann Arbor, and head coach Kyle Whittingham said that he gives Underwood an A-plus for his performances thus far in fall camp. His offensive coordinator, Jason Beck, won't go that far, but he's noted that Underwood is doing precisely what they've asked of him thus far.

"Bryce has had 13 good practices," Beck said. "Just working hard, consistent. There's not these big ups and downs. In the spring there were some highs and some lows. This has been 13 good practices. He's been really steady. Tons to improve. It's hard to get an A-plus, just in terms of, I just remember the negatives. That's all that stands out is the questions you get wrong. But he's had a nice camp and done a nice job."

The big thing for Underwood has been improving both his mechanics and his decision-making. As far as Beck sees it, those things are improving, but even though it is a concerted effort, his development isn't as much about looking under the hood at every granular detail as it's been about getting the offense right and then working from there.

"When we got here, it was not, 'Hey, here's the footwork and this is what we do,'" Beck said. "It was install and go through spring, and now as we've gone through spring, OK, here's some things that I've seen consistently we want to work on. And he's made improvements in that, and it's shown off, and it's looked better and allowed him to make some strides. However, that stuff is like the last thing you're thinking of.

You're just, 'Hey, here's the play and here's my read and here's the coverage and here's. . .' you're not thinking about that. And so whenever you start playing, and bullets become live and real and all that, there's always that element of you're going to revert to -- I don't know what the word is, but the subconscious. Just whatever you're doing without thinking. And he's been really -- anyway, so he's made nice strides. We'll continue to emphasize it and play to his strengths and put him in the best situation to be successful."

One thing Beck notes is that Underwood, on tape from last year, was trying to do too much at times. He still sees that, and while he's not trying to coach that out of him entirely, it's about being smarter when he does try to put the offense on his back by running the football or scrambling out of the pocket.

The expectation is that Underwood will be a run threat -- Beck acknowledges that he prefers a running quarterback -- but he wants him to be smart about what he does when he has the ball in his hands.

"Just make the routine plays. Make the normal plays. Make the routine plays," Beck said. "When everything breaks down, extend it, scramble, get what you can get. We've worked a lot of scramble drill with training with that and those decisions as well."

There are just over two weeks until the September 5 season opener against Western Michigan at The Big House. Fall camp will continue for another week and a half before officially transitioning to game week.

title: Colts' Daniel Jones has more at stake in Indianapolis than you think
description: The Indianapolis Colts have locked in Daniel Jones, but just for now.
fullText:
Colts' Daniel Jones has more at stake in Indianapolis than you think originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Daniel Jones is back with the Indianapolis Colts for another run. He's healthy again, which is huge. He's also coming off a season that saw great numbers, before he was injured.

Last season, Jones appeared in 13 games before he got injured. He completed 261 of 384 passes for 3,101 yards and 19 touchdowns. Those aren't shabby numbers.

So, Jones is back, and there's lots of excitement in the Colts' camp about what he can do this season. But, this season is actually extremely crucial to Jones for his future with the team.

In a feature released on Thursday, Dan Graziano of ESPN makes quarterback predictions for the fresh season and beyond, including draft ideas. He says this is a big year for Jones.

Basically, Jones is playing for his long-term life in Indianapolis. The Colts have committed two years and $88 million to his deal, with more than $60 million guaranteed. So, they made a big bet on him. But, he has to prove that he's just as stellar after his injury and the guy they should sign for the long term.

His projection is actually a dismal one. He sees Jones getting injured again and being "in and out of the lineup throughout the season." That means the Colts will "have to decide next offseason whether to bring him back or move on. Their final win-loss record, and whatever decisions ownership makes about the futures of the coaching staff and the front office, will likely determine Jones' future in Indianapolis."

It's not just about if he can have a good season. It's about whether the Colts have finally found their franchise quarterback and the face of the team for years to come.

title: Seven defenders on the books - why Arsenal still want Konsa
description: Arsenal have already spent more than £100m this summer as they look to defend their Premier League title - so why do they want Ezri Konsa as well?
fullText:
Arsenal are not standing still as they look to defend their Premier League title.

The Gunners have spent more than £100m already, bringing in Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle (£75m) and Club Brugge winger Christos Tzolis (£34m) during this transfer window.

And they are now set to bring in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for around £51m.

It may seem strange that Arsenal - who have seven senior defenders - want to bring in another established centre-back, but there are reasons why Mikel Arteta has decided to go for the England international.

Last season, Arsenal's extremely well drilled backline, aided by the effective partnership of William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes, helped them win their first title in 22 years. They only conceded 27 league goals.

But half of their title-winning defence is not going to be fit for the first part of the season.

Saliba has been ruled out for an 'extended period' with a long-term back issue which he had been managing last season and which ended his World Cup with France early.

Jurrien Timber, Arsenal's first-choice right-back, is also out for the opening weeks of the season with a groin problem that caused him to pull out of the Netherlands World Cup squad.

That leaves Ben White, who has had his own fitness issues in recent seasons, as Arsenal's only fit right-back and 21-year-old Cristhian Mosquera as the only right sided centre back to partner Gabriel Magalhaes.

It could be argued that Arsenal, who also made defender Piero Hincapie's loan deal permanent this summer, could be able to cope without signing another defender.

But Arteta does not seem to like fielding two left-footed players at centre-back - which would happen if White got injured and Mosquera had to move to right-back.

Riccardo Calafiori is preferred at left-back by Arteta, because of the unpredictability he brings to the Arsenal attack. Hincapie is left-sided too.

Highly rated 16-year-old academy defender Marli Salmon is also on the books but is most likely to be used sparingly in cup competitions as he continues to develop.

Before Arsenal moved for Konsa, they considered signing Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah who can play at right-back and as a right-sided centre-back.

Konsa, like Guimaraes, is 28 and in the prime of his career. A seasoned international centre-back, he lifted the Europa League with Villa last season.

He is one of his country's most reliable performers, starting seven of England's eight games at the World Cup.

His Premier League numbers show why Arsenal were so keen to bring Konsa in.

He was ranked as having the best ground duel success (73.1%) and best passing accuracy (95%) of all defenders in the Premier League last season.

His passing accuracy was the best of any player too, while he was also ranked first out of all Premier League outfield players to contest more than 20 ground duels in the league last season.

He also ranked fifth of all defenders in the league for ball carries of more than five metres - and he carried his passing accuracy into the World Cup, as in his seven starts, he registered a 97% pass completion rate.

Many Arsenal fans are wondering if Konsa will play regularly when Saliba and Gabriel are fit.

Arteta's first-choice backline of Timber, Saliba, Gabriel and Calafiori appears hard to break into, on paper.

But the Gunners played 63 games in all competitions as they won the title, reached the final of the Champions League, the final of the Carabao Cup and the quarter-final of the FA Cup.

Arsenal were plagued by injuries during the campaign and Arteta is trying to avoid those issues this time.

In the aftermath of the Champions League final, Arteta was quick to say that the Gunners need to be "very ambitious, very fast, and very smart" to build on their Premier League win.

Arsenal spent £250m last summer. The arrival of Konsa will take this summer's outlay to over £150m.

Arteta has some of the best depth of quality in Europe to call on, in a squad worth £1.19bn according to Transfermarkt.

When asked about the perfect number of players in his squad, Arteta said there are variables he takes into account.

"It depends on the ability and the history of those players," Arteta said.

"I think there is a lot of factors that count. Twenty two outfield players and three goalkeepers of what is enough, or maybe you know more.

"You need to understand what happened in the previous season, the injury record of those players, the versatility of certain players.

"But I'm sure we're going to hit the right number to have a bit of both a lot of competition with the right level of cooperation in the team and everybody feeling important."

Arsenal want to be one of the global powerhouses in world football.

Chief executive Richard Garlick said in an interview with the Times that joining the world's superclubs is "the goal - that's the ambition".

The Gunners are actively exploring how to increase their revenue off the pitch and are looking at stadium expansion plans.

Garlick, in an interview with BBC Sport, acknowledged that the "pool of players is smaller now than it was a few years ago if we're going to improve". In other words, as Arsenal have got better, it has become more difficult to find players who will improve them.

They are still in the market for a forward and have a long-term interest in Julian Alvarez. They have also monitored 21-year-old forward Kenan Yildiz from Juventus.

But after Konsa's arrival, if another player does come in, expect the signing to lift club to another level.

title: Where Florida football lands in preseason bowl projections
description: Florida football is projected to face off against an in-state rival in CBS Sports' preseason bowl projections.
fullText:
The Florida Gators look to return to the postseason after missing a bowl game for the fourth time since 2013 last season.

With the 2026 college football season quickly approaching, bowl projections are beginning to take shape, previewing an early look at how the 43-game bowl slate could unfold. Plenty can change between now and December.

Florida enters the season under first-year head coach Jon Sumrall, who has never missed postseason football in his career. The program hopes to reestablish itself as a contender in the SEC with new play-calling and roster construction, though there are still plenty of questions to be answered before the schedule is played out.

CBS Sports' latest bowl projections provide an early indication of where they could be headed if a successful 2026 campaign is put together. The Gators are projected to face off against South Florida in the Cure Bowl.

The matchup would allow the program to face an in-state opponent it has faced a few times over the years. Since 2010, the Gators have held a 3-1 record against South Florida, with the Bulls' lone victory coming last year when they upset Florida, 18-16, in Gainesville.

USF participated in the Cure Bowl last season, losing to Old Dominion, 24-10.

Florida has controlled most of their matchups in the past, but a potential bowl matchup would also mark the first meeting between Florida and South Florida in the Sumrall era and would give the Gators a chance to get back on track against the in-state opponent.

title: Mahmic would provide Celtic with a key trait that’s been missing
description: Ermin Mahmic would provide Celtic with a key trait that’s been missing for quite some time. He’d be an exciting signing…With Arne Engels now a West Ham United player, after his £25 million move...
fullText:
With Arne Engels now a West Ham United player, after his £25 million move, and Reo Hatate seeking a move elsewhere, it's imperative that we add some more quality to our low on numbers midfield.

Mika Baur has of course arrived, but we are still in need of more additions all the same.

One of the several midfield players Celtic have been credited with an interest in is Bosnian international Ermin Mahmic. Mahmec who starred for his nation in the recent World Cup, plays his club football for Czech side Slovan Liberec, and is undoubtedly a player of great potential.

Having studied the 22 year old quite a bit since he was credited as a player of interest, it's clear to see that he's more than just a playmaker, with his ability to score from outside the box also forming a huge part of his game.

The youngster regularly likes to have a pop from distance, and more often than not he hits the target, with the ball either ending up in the back of the net, or resulting in the keeper having to make a save.

The old objective of 'if you don't shoot you don't score' is sadly a dying art in the modern game, and we could certainly do with someone of Mahmec's skill in that regard.

We have Benjamin Nygren, who of course gets his fair share of goals form the middle of the park, but we also need someone who possesses a threat from outside the box in terms of shooting from distance.

We face packed defensive lines on a regular occurrence, so having someone who was not only able to open up defences, but someone capable of finding the net from distance, a bit like Arne Engels did in last season's Scottish cup final.

Mahmic is certainly someone who would fit our transfer strategy. He's young, he's an international and he'll only get better.

Martin O'Neill, Celtic 3 LASK 0, Champions league Playoff, Celtic Park, 19 August 2026.

(Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Martin O'Neill went out of his way to point out that Celtic have brought in more than they have spent in the transfer market this summer, a subtle way of telling the Board he wants money spent on additions as Celtic now have one foot in the Champions League draw a week today.

Ermin Mahmic is clearly a player of particular interest, he wants to come if reports are to be believed, now we just need to ambition from the boardroom to get these remaining deals across the line before the summer transfer window closes on 3rd September.

title: Raiders Film Room: Kubiak has a plan for Mike Washington JR
description: Las Vegas Raiders new running back Mike Washington Jr. had a big day and fans found out how he will be used by Klint Kubiak
fullText:
The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Mike Washington Jr. in the fourth round of the 2026 draft. This shows the Raiders have a vision for playing smash-mouth football with a mix of Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty.

Washington Jr. comes from a system at Arkansas that was different from Klint Kubiak's. At Arkansas, Washington Jr. ran a gap scheme primarily, whereas Kubiak prefers a wide zone scheme. The question became what plan would best maximize Washington Jr.'s talents at the next level.

The first preseason game of 2026 gave fans a taste of what it could look like when Washington Jr. is the running back. He finished with 63 yards on six carries with an explosive 53-yard run in the second quarter.

Kubiak's plan is to get Washington Jr. in space. Of the six carries, three were wide zone or a toss play. An example is below in the 2nd quarter. Raiders run an outside zone play to help get him in space to the outside. Washington Jr. does a good job reading and getting outside with patience, allowing blocks to develop, and gets 4 yards.

All the other runs were gap scheme runs or duo. Duo is a run where the running back starts his flow on the strong-side A gap. Then Washington Jr. reads the blocks and chooses which gap he wants to hit. Of course, on this run there was excellent blocking in front of him to allow him to get to the second level. He does the rest and ends with a 53 yard run.

The blocking on this Mike Washington Jr run. 

Grant, Mafi, and Meredith set it up. 

Jack Bech with the crack opens it up late, and Washington Jr does the rest. pic.twitter.com/4pjdAWrgtC

Washington Jr. exhibited the home run ability that makes him an intriguing one-two punch with Jeanty. Kubiak has a plan for the young running back, and it is off to a great start.

title: Kansas State football starting left tackle John Pastore out for season
description: Kansas State football coach Collin Klein said the Wildcats’ starting left tackle will miss the season with an injury.
fullText:
MANHATTAN — Kansas State football starting left tackle John Pastore will miss the season after suffering a lower body injury.

Wildcats coach Collin Klein confirmed Pastore's injury during an impromptu statement he delivered on Thursday, Aug. 20.

Pastore entered 2026 as the team's lone returning starter along the offensive line. A second-team All-Big 12 performer a year ago, Pastore was a consensus preseason All-Big 12 player heading into the year.

Pastore took over left tackle full-time in 2025 after Ohio State transfer George Fitzpatrick suffered a preseason medical emergency that sidelined him for the entire year. At 6-foot-6, 302 pounds, Pastore excelled. He allowed 16 pressures on 360 pass-blocking opportunities, allowing just one sack and two hits on the quarterback.

Entering the year, Pastore was already being teased as a potential NFL Draft target in 2027.

Under the NCAA's new age-based eligibility rules, medical hardship waivers were eliminated, meaning he won't have an opportunity to return to the Wildcats next year unless he challenges the new rules in court.

As far as those with experience, Auburn transfer Tyler Johnson may be the first one to look at. He's listed at 6-foot-6, 312 pounds as he enters his senior year. Pro Football Focus advanced stats have not been favorable to him, particularly in the 2024 season when he started the year at left tackle, only to be benched three games in. He played seven snaps last season at right tackle and gave up a sack.

Someone who could sneak his way into a starting role right away is freshman Oliver Miller, who has received as much praise as anyone on the roster since the spring. Miller, listed at 6-foot-6 and 294 pounds, was teased by Klein last week that he was already in the middle of several competitions and would likely be among the few freshmen to see the field right away.

Klein probably didn't imagine having him as a starter at left tackle this early, but the situation might have presented the opportunity. Another possibility at the position could be Gus Hawkins, the likely starter at right tackle, but it's more likely he remains where he's been.

Klein also noted that Fitzpatrick will miss the season.

title: Is Seahawks OC Brian Fleury on the hot seat for the 2026 NFL season?
description: Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury will have all eyes on him to lead the team’s offense next season in place of Klint Kubiak.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks will be under the microscope to see whether or not they will defend their Super Bowl title next season.

Sam Darnold approaches the third year of his prime with a chance to solidify himself as the caliber of player that he's shown himself to be. Rashid Shaheed will get the chance to prove that his downtick in numbers since being traded to Seattle midway through last season is behind him. Anthony Bradford will need to right the ship after his down year in 2025, and new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury will be tasked with running the offense. Many players and coaches may end up finding themselves on the hot seat.

CBS Sports' Zachary Pereles named Fleury as the member of the Seahawks who will be on the hot seat for next season.

"It's pretty straightforward here: Brian Fleury is a first-time offensive coordinator taking over for the reigning Super Bowl champions," Pereles said. "His predecessor, Klint Kubiak, did a terrific job with QB Sam Darnold and WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but now he's off to Las Vegas."

The Seahawks will need to adjust to not having star running back Kenneth Walker III any more. With rookie RB Jadarian Price set to handle the lion share of responsibilities in the ground game to begin the season, especially with Zach Charbonnet working his way back from injury, as well as Rashid Shaheed being in line for a larger role, Fleury will be tasked with orchestrating the offense with precision.

Comparisons to Kubiak will likely spring up throughout the year. However, ensuring that the Seahawks pile on yards and points that lead to wins will factor in to Fleury's success on the season.

title: Andy Reid delivers latest Patrick Mahomes injury update ahead of Chiefs’ upcoming clash
description: Patrick Mahomes will not play in the Kansas City Chiefs’ pre-season game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Andy Reid has confirmed the decision.
fullText:
Patrick Mahomes will not play in the Kansas City Chiefs' pre-season game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Andy Reid has confirmed the decision.

That comes after the Chiefs opened their pre-season with a 12–20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game Mahomes also missed.

Reid is protecting his franchise quarterback, and there is a good reason. Mahomes is working his way back from a serious knee injury.

Justin Fields will start instead and is expected to play into the second quarter on Saturday. Trey Smith, Josh Simmons and Ashton Gillotte will also sit the game out, per ESPN's Nate Taylor.

Reid had already hinted at this approach. Speaking a week before the Rams meeting, he said:

"There's a pretty good chance I don't play him [in the first pre-season game]. Percentages are leaning that way. I don't know if I'll play him the second or third game; I don't know that, but the percentages likely lean against doing that. We've got new people in those other positions behind him that need some work, and so the more reps they get, the better."

The caution makes sense when you remember how the injury happened. Mahomes was scrambling during the fourth quarter of the December 14, 2025 clash with the Los Angeles Chargers when an awkward hit buckled his left knee.

Tests confirmed a complete tear of the ACL and significant damage to the LCL. He underwent dual-ligament reconstruction surgery and has spent seven months recovering.

On July 24, 2026, Reid announced Mahomes was fully cleared for 11-on-11 contact at the start of training camp. Teammates have said he looks sharp and shows 'zero limitations', although he has been wearing a brace on his left knee.

Keeping him out of at least two pre-season games removes any risk of contact before the real thing. After Tampa Bay, the Chiefs host the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on Friday, August 28.

But the only date that truly matters is September 14. Mahomes will be under centre when Kansas City open the regular season against the Denver Broncos.

title: Western Kentucky DL enters transfer portal after gaining eligibility
description: Western Kentucky defensive lineman Victory Vaka has entered the transfer portal after earning a fifth season of eligibility.
fullText:
Western Kentucky defensive lineman Victory Vaka has entered the transfer portal after earning another season of eligibility, according to Chris Hummer of 247Sports. He was granted a temporary injunction on Wednesday, allowing him to enter.

He needed a temporary injunction after his eligibility was jeopardized by an off-field matter. He took time away from the Western Kentucky program to attend the funeral of his mom, Sarah Mataele, after she died unexpectedly on April 2.

According to Vaka, via Alaina Morris of the Louisville Courier Journal, an assistant strength coach called him nine days before the funeral and told the defensive lineman he needed to return to Bowling Green by June. On May 26, his position coach called him to ask where he was, and Travis Taylor, the chief of staff at Western Kentucky, told Vaka and his agent one day later that the program had decided to revoke his scholarship.

Multiple teams were interested in his transfer, but NCAA rules prevented him from using the portal because of how he left. Western Kentucky designated Vaka as a "failure to report," a disciplinary dismissal that made him ineligible for the exemption.

Vaka, a former three-star recruit, started his career at BYU. He didn't play at BYU, but he played two seasons at College of the Canyons and the 2025 season at Texas Southern before transferring to Western Kentucky for his final season of eligibility. Now, he's free to go to a place where he can compete for a starting job.

title: Former Spurs champion says rejecting San Antonio's $10M offer was a huge mistake
description: Stephen Jackson looked back on his decision to reject the Spurs' $10 million contract, admitting it may have cost him multiple NBA championships.
fullText:
Former Spurs champion says rejecting San Antonio's $10M offer was a huge mistake originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Stephen Jackson's NBA career didn't begin exactly as he had envisioned, but the San Antonio Spurs quickly recognized his value as a reliable two-way wing. The organization believed Jackson had the tools to defend multiple positions while providing timely outside shooting alongside Tim Duncan.

After injuries limited him for most of the 2001-02 season, Jackson enjoyed a breakthrough campaign in 2002-03. Former Spurs head coach Gregg Popovich inserted him into the starting lineup, and the move paid off. Jackson averaged 12.8 points per game during the playoff, playing a key role in San Antonio's championship run.

Following that title-winning season, Jackson believed he had earned a significant payday. He was confident that he was emerging as one of the league's rising stars and declined the Spurs' three-year, $10 million contract offer in hopes of securing a larger deal elsewhere.

Looking back, Jackson admits he would make a different decision.

"I wanted my big contract," Jackson said in "All The Smoke" podcast. "I felt like I deserved a big contract… If I could rewind back, I would have took that three-year, $10 million… I would have been on a championship team."

Passing on the Spurs' offer was a gamble, but Jackson eventually recovered financially. A breakout stint with the Atlanta Hawks helped boost his value, and later trades throughout his career allowed him to earn considerably more than the contract he originally turned down.

However, Jackson believes the biggest cost wasn't financial, instead, it was the championships he may have missed.

"I probably won two more championships, then I would have got a crazy bag," Jackson said. "I didn't understand the business at the time, so I was upset with them not getting my bag."

If Jackson accepted the three-year extension, he would have remained with the Spurs from 2003 through 2006, staying alongside Tim Duncan, Manu Ginobili and Tony Parker during one of the most dominant stretches of San Antonio's dynasty.

title: OU football coach Brent Venables agrees to two-year contract extension
description: Oklahoma football and Brent Venables have agreed to a two-year contract extension, keeping the head coach in Norman through 2031.
fullText:
NORMAN — Fresh off a College Football Playoff appearance, Oklahoma football has locked up its head coach.

The Sooners and coach Brent Venables have agreed to a new two-year contract extension, the program announced Thursday. The deal will keep Venables in Norman through the 2031 season.

"Coach Venables is elite at building culture — not just in the locker room, but throughout the entire program," athletic director Roger Denny said in a statement. "I believe strongly in Coach Venables, in the culture he has built and in the structure we have in place around our football program."

More: OU football RB Xavier Robinson finally healthy, ready to show improvements for Sooners

Coach Venables has agreed to a contract extension through the 2031 season.

» https://t.co/u21BxukzqR pic.twitter.com/2UMlbzUSV6

Venables, 55, is entering his fifth season as Oklahoma's head coach. He led the Sooners to their first CFP appearance since 2019 last season, when OU earned the No. 8 seed and hosted a first-round game.

The new deal will average $10.5 million annually, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel.

The Sooners also won 10 regular-season games for the second time under Venables in 2025. OU enters this season ranked No. 9 in the preseason coaches poll and No. 10 in the AP poll.

"My family and I love Oklahoma," Venables said in a statement. "This is our home, and we are deeply grateful for the way the Oklahoma family has embraced and supported us."

A former longtime defensive coordinator at OU and Clemson, Venables has coached in eight national championship games between his time at the two schools, winning titles with the Sooners in 2000 and Tigers in 2016 and 2018.

The OU Board of Regents will next meet Sept. 15-16 to finalize the new deal.
